why: Simulate the calls with counters instead of re-scanning the board: map each value to its cell, keep a count of marked cells per row, per column and on the main diagonal, and stop the first time a counter reaches n.
hints: Rechecking every line after every call is O(n^2) per call. What changes when one cell is marked?
Only that cell's row, column and (if r == c) the diagonal can become complete. Keep rows[r], cols[c], diag counters.
Build value -> (r, c), then for call k: skip unknown or already-marked values, bump the counters, return [1, k] when one hits n. Otherwise [0, len(called)]. O(n^2 + calls).
pitfalls: A repeated value must not be counted twice: keep a marked set.
Values not on the board still count as calls (k is the 1-based call index).
Only the main diagonal counts, not the anti-diagonal.
